approach:
RAISE AT THE ONE READ, CATCH ONLY WHERE A REASON CAN BE CARRIED, LET EVERYTHING ELSE PROPAGATE. No new type, no interface change beyond the two Tim named (ReadLinkTarget, IsLinkTarget). Exceptions reused: IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException (PathCanonicalizer.cs:49-55 already throws IOException for a cycle).

WHICH EXCEPTIONS MEAN WHAT (I probed real .NET 10 on this macOS box with FileInfo/DirectoryInfo.LinkTarget): a regular file, a directory, a missing path, a path with a missing parent (nope/x/y) and a path under a regular file (f/x) ALL return null and raise nothing. A dangling link and a self-loop return their target. So on Unix an absent path or a not-yet-created parent never raises from the read; the null-vs-raise split is made by .NET, not by us. PathCanonicalizer reads every ancestor of every path, so a wholesale raise is NOT a risk on the evidence: ordinary writes under a not-yet-created parent keep getting null. Therefore any IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException that reaches a caller from the read means "an entry that is there but cannot be read" and is treated as an unreadable link. Absent is never signalled by an exception from this read.
  Windows not probed (no Windows host here): .NET's Windows path can surface FileNotFoundException/DirectoryNotFoundException (IOException subclasses) for a missing path. To keep absent=null on Windows, ReadLinkTarget gets ONE narrow catch, `catch (Exception e) when (e is FileNotFoundException or DirectoryNotFoundException) { return null; }`, which is an answer (absent) and not a swallow, and the contract's own null definition includes absent. Everything else propagates. This goes beyond the contract's 'remove both catch blocks' and needs Tim's yes (or must be dropped if a Windows CI probe shows .NET already returns null); I list it as a risk and an open item, not a silent default.
  BIG CAVEAT: on this macOS probe a directory with mode 000 holding a link still returned null from LinkTarget (no EACCES raised). So on POSIX the raise may essentially never fire in the real implementation; the real on-disk raise test can likely only be written for Windows, and the POSIX proof has to come from the test double. This is Ground's open question 4 answered partly: it does NOT raise for a no-permission parent on macOS.

WHERE EACH CATCH GOES (all catch both types, carry exception.Message, name the path):
1. PlatformFileSystemBase.ReadLinkTarget: remove both catches (plus the narrow absent catch above if approved). IsLinkTarget stays `ReadLinkTarget(p) is not null` and inherits the raise. Update IPlatformFileSystem docs at :28 and :36 (null = not a link or absent; unreadable link raises IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException).
2. PathCanonicalizer.Resolve/Canonicalize: NO catch. It returns CanonicalPath, so it cannot return a denial; adding a catch would force a swallow or a signature change. The exception propagates exactly like the existing cycle IOException (one precedent, one behaviour). Document it on IPathCanonicalizer.Canonicalize.
3. FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync (FileGuard.cs:346): the one catch that matters. Wrap `_canonicalizer.Canonicalize(rawPath)` in catch IOException / UnauthorizedAccessException and return Verdict.Deny($"Cannot canonicalize '{rawPath}', failing closed: {exception.Message}"). It has no catch today, so an unreadable link (and the existing cycle) escapes uncaught from Pre. Must be one shared private helper if more than one catch block would repeat the Deny text (DRY; use an exception filter `when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)` to be one clause). The other Canonicalize callers need nothing: CaptureAsync/Post already convert both exceptions to CaptureFailed/Deny with the message (FileGuard.cs:90-100, :125-129) and ProtectedFileScanner sits inside that; DirectoryPrefixMatcher, ExactPathMatcher, RegionMapRegistry and GuardEngine.cs:48/109/111 run at engine construction on fixed config paths, so a raise there fails the start loudly, which is correct (not caught).
4. SymlinkOps.EnsurePointsTo: no catch; the raise now stops it BEFORE MakeLinkTarget, ending today's behaviour where an unreadable link is overwritten. CreationHelper.RepairLink (:235-243) adds IOException to its existing UnauthorizedAccessException catch, merged into ONE filter clause `catch (Exception e) when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)` returning RepairOutcome.NotRepairable(e.Message). Caveat: MakeLinkTarget already throws IOException on a failed rename, so RepairLink now also reports that as NotRepairable instead of crashing; that is correct and I will say so in the contract.
5. BinSymlinkCondition.DetectInstalled and CurrentSymlinkCondition.DetectInstalled: catch the two types around ReadLinkTarget and return ConditionState.CannotVerify($"{path} is an unreadable link: {message}"), NOT Broken. CannotVerify already exists and is used for unreadable state.json/.gitignore (GitignoreCondition:29, VersionStampCondition:32,43); Broken would invite a repair that overwrites a link we could not read. The two copies of the read-and-compare must share one helper (the compare is already duplicated across the two; fold read+catch+compare into one internal method on the shared base or a static helper next to MachinePaths so the catch is written once). Ground's claim that Broken is the carrier is the contract's wording; CannotVerify is the better fit and matches the project rule that cannot-tell is never reported as checked-OK or as a repair target. Flag this as a contract wording change to confirm.
6. InstallIntegrity.HasCurrentEntry: no catch inside it (an unreadable `current` link is neither present nor absent, so it has no honest bool). Catch once at the call site of FindInstallRoot in the integrity Check (it already returns IntegrityReport.Deny with a reason, and already has catch IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException precedent at :90-98): IntegrityReport.Deny($"could not locate the install root; a `current` link is unreadable: {message}"). Fail-closed with the reason carried.
7. PosixFileSystem.MakeLinkTarget/RemoveLinkTarget and WindowsFileSystem.MakeLinkTarget/RemoveLinkTarget: no catch. They call IsLinkTarget to decide 'refuse a real entry'; a raise now stops them from treating an unreadable link as a real entry or overwriting it. IOException from MakeLinkTarget is already their documented shape. Update the IPlatformFileSystem MakeLinkTarget/RemoveLinkTarget docs to list it. Optional tidy only if Tim wants: WindowsFileSystem.MakeLinkTarget reads IsLinkTarget twice (:73, :80); one local would be a single read, but it is outside this issue.
8. TEST DOUBLES: InMemoryFileSystemStore, ManagedPlatformFileSystem and the base delegation have no catch and therefore propagate a raising base; nothing to change for propagation. But the store cannot simulate an unreadable link, and no mocking library exists in tests. Callers 3-6 (and the contract's acceptance item 4) cannot be proven in unit tests without a way to raise. Needs Tim's explicit approval (global rule 2: new seam on a test double): add to InMemoryFileSystemStore an overlay mark 'unreadable link' at a path (AddUnreadableLink(path, exception)) so ReadLinkTarget/IsLinkTarget throw the given IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException, exposed through the existing test-helper builder. Without it, the POSIX proof is impossible (probe above) and only Windows gets an on-disk test.

TESTS (to be written by TDD, listed for the contract): ReadLinkTarget on non-link/absent/missing-parent still null (existing three tests stay); unreadable link raises the exact type (double seam, plus Windows on-disk where an ACL can be arranged); Pre on a write whose path crosses an unreadable link is Deny with the exception message in the reason (not an uncaught exception, not Allow); EnsurePointsTo on an unreadable link does not call MakeLinkTarget and RepairLink returns NotRepairable with the message for BOTH exception types; Bin/Current conditions return CannotVerify with the message, never Broken 'points at ''' ; integrity Check returns Deny with reason; Posix/Windows MakeLinkTarget/RemoveLinkTarget raise instead of overwriting. Each case named in test output.

approach:
Two channels, split at one seam. The AGENT channel is the Verdict.Deny text. It is composed ONLY in FileGuard from fixed string literals, never from an exception, a Loaded.Why, or a path. The TRUSTED channel is the approved warning sink behind ISystemServices (decision `sweep`), which is where Tim reads the exact cause. The exact cause is built at the place that sees it and goes to the sink there, so no exact text travels toward the agent.

Verified against live code. (a) IGrantStore.GetActiveGrantsAsync returns Task<IReadOnlyList<Grant>>, and FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync (FileGuard.cs ~340-365) is its consumer and the only Verdict producer on that path ("A write to a System path requires an authorizing grant: {rawPath}"). (b) GrantStore.TryLoadAsync catches only JsonException, FormatException and IOException with no variable, and invalid-signature and expiry return null with no cause. (c) GuardEngine.LoadGrantPublicKey has three bare catches plus two Empty returns (absent file, wrong length) and runs at composition time, where no Verdict exists. (d) FileGuard already puts exception.Message and a path into CaptureFailed (lines 95, 99, 192, 196, 221, 225). So FileGuard's existing capture reasons already leak exact text and paths to wherever CaptureFailed is rendered. I did not verify that rendering; the worker must. (e) The contract's group 3 sentence says FileGuard 383-387 "carries the exception's message into Verdict.Deny". That contradicts decision `tell` (no raw exception text reaches the agent), so the exception message goes to the sink and the Deny stays fixed text. (f) The warning sink does not exist in src yet (grep finds no sink type). It is built under group 4, and group 3 reuses that one sink instead of making another.

Per-place carrying:
1. GrantStore.TryLoadAsync. It stays private and returns Loaded<Grant?>. The invalid-signature and expired branches set Why to a fixed cause string such as "grant <id> signature not accepted" or "grant <id> expired at <time>". The three catches name their exception and set Why to "<file name>: <exception type>: <message>". UnauthorizedAccessException is currently NOT caught here and escapes GetActiveGrantsAsync. Add it to the catch list so that an unreadable grant file becomes a rejected grant with a reason, matching the other IO failures. Do not widen it past the three IO-class exceptions already present.
2. IGrantStore.GetActiveGrantsAsync returns Task<Loaded<IReadOnlyList<Grant>>>. Value is the good grants. Why is null when every grant file was accepted or the directory was simply empty. Otherwise Why is the exact causes joined, one per rejected file, and also covers "no key configured" and "grant directory absent". This is an interface change Tim approved by name. Update the IGrantStore XML doc in the same edit.
3. FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync takes Value for coverage. The Deny text stays a fixed literal and never interpolates Why. To tell "not configured" from "not accepted" without a second type, GrantStore sets Why only for rejections and uses a fixed prefix constant for the key-absent case. FileGuard picks one of two literals by whether Why is null. If the worker finds this cannot be done without parsing Why, use the single literal "no grant is in effect for this path (grants are not configured, or none was accepted)". That satisfies acceptance 8a, which allows not-configured or not-accepted.
4. Who writes the exact Why to the sink. FileGuardServices carries no ISystemServices today. The least-new-surface route is for GrantStore.Create to hold services.Warnings (the sink on the container it already receives). GrantStore reports each exact cause to the sink as it builds the Loaded. FileGuard then never sees or forwards Why for text, only for "was there a cause". That keeps the exact text from reaching the Verdict-building class at all.
5. GuardEngine.LoadGrantPublicKey returns Loaded<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>. This follows decision `trust`. Key file absent returns (Empty, "grant public key file not present: grants switched off") and the sink receives that line as information. A key that exists but is not decodable, is the wrong length, or is unreadable RAISES a trust-configuration failure with the exact cause, and CreatePipeline lets it escape to the composition root. The exact cause appears on stderr there, which is Tim's channel and not the agent's. Nothing here returns Empty for a corrupt key. That replaces today's silent "wrong anchor means no grants" with a loud failure.
6. Ed25519SignatureService.Verify keeps bool and never throws (documented, and ISignatureService.Verify is unchanged). The two catches (ArgumentException, CryptoException) and the wrong-length early return name the exception and report it to the sink. Because Boundaries is below Engine, the sink must be a Boundaries-visible abstraction on the same ISystemServices container. The worker must check whether Ed25519SignatureService can be given it without an upward dependency (memory rule: dependencies point one way). If it cannot, the reason is recovered one layer up and never invented here. GrantStore classifies a false Verify result as "signature not accepted" for the sink, and the Ed25519 catches that cannot reach a sink are left as the documented false. In that case the Ed25519 line in acceptance 8 needs Tim's sign-off, so I flag it instead of deciding it.
7. FileGuard 383-387. The first-attempt catches name their exception and pass it to the sink as a "retrying" warning. The final failure Deny stays the existing fixed string, "Post could not scan or read the tree after a retry; failing closed with no effects.", with the exception detail sent to the sink only.
8. WindowsUserPresence 154/175 and BuildOutputSkipRule 47/51. Both name the exception and report to the sink. Presence keeps its enum result, so the detail goes to the sink and is not added to PresenceResult.Detail (that is shown to the user at the prompt boundary, and I have not proven it never reaches the agent). BuildOutputSkipRule keeps returning false and warns, since the failure means "descend", not a denial.

Where each message is composed: the exact text is composed at the catch (it is the only place that has the exception and the path). The coarse text is composed at FileGuard from literals. Loaded.Why is by definition trusted-only text. The rule is that no code path takes Why or an exception into a Verdict.
keySteps: Add record Loaded<T>(T Value, string? Why) in AgentGuard.Abstractions, matching how the other records there are written, and nowhere else. Confirm with grep that no other 'value plus reason' type exists (the ledger says none does).

Change IGrantStore.GetActiveGrantsAsync to Task<Loaded<IReadOnlyList<Grant>>> and update the XML doc. Update the only two production callers (FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync and ReconcileAsync) and the tests that call it.

Change GrantStore: TryLoadAsync returns Loaded<Grant?>. Name every caught exception and add UnauthorizedAccessException to the three IO-class catches. Set a fixed Why for invalid signature, expired grant, wrong-length key, empty key and missing directory. Aggregate the Whys into the list result and send each exact cause to the sink.

Change GuardEngine.LoadGrantPublicKey to Loaded<ReadOnlyMemory<byte>>. An absent file is (Empty, Why) meaning grants switched off. A key that is corrupt, the wrong length or unreadable raises a trust-configuration failure with the exact cause, and the composition root surfaces it loudly.

Keep ISignatureService.Verify's signature and its never-throws doc. Name the exceptions in Ed25519SignatureService and report them to the sink if Boundaries can reach it without an upward dependency. If it cannot, bring Tim the one gap (an Ed25519 catch with no channel) and do not choose.

FileGuard.PrecheckWriteAsync composes only fixed literals for the agent's Deny, selected by whether Why is null, and never interpolates Why. FileGuard.TryReadCurrentAsync names both exceptions on both attempts, sends the detail to the sink, and keeps the fixed Deny.
Windows presence and BuildOutputSkipRule: name the exception and report it to the sink, keeping their current result types.
Reuse the single warning sink approved in group 4 for every group 3 report. Do not create a second sink, logger or diagnostic type.

Tests, each named in the output. Acceptance 8: six assertions, one per place, that the exact cause reaches the sink. 8a: one test that feeds a grant file path with an absolute path and a raw exception message into every failure mode, then asserts the Deny text equals one of the fixed literals and contains neither the path nor the message. 8b: three Verify cases that return false and do not throw. 8c: key absent versus key wrong length. 8d: Loaded carries Value and Why, and expired and corrupt each give a non-empty Why.

rulesToAdd.rule: A Verdict.Deny/Warn/Block reason string in AgentGuard.Engine must not be built from an exception, an exception's Message, or a Loaded<T>.Why. It may use only constants and the path the agent already supplied. The analyzer is a data-flow rule over interpolated or concatenated string arguments to Verdict factory methods, flagging any reference whose type derives from System.Exception, any use of .Message or .ToString() on an exception, and any member access to Loaded<T>.Why. Kind: Roslyn operation analyzer on IInvocationOperation for Verdict.Deny/Warn, with an allow-list of constants.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: A later change copies the exact cause into the text the guarded agent sees. That turns the denial into an oracle (invalid signature versus expired versus wrong key) and leaks absolute paths. Decision `tell` forbids this, and today only a test would notice.

rulesToAdd.rule: No catch clause under src may be empty, comment-only, or declare no exception variable AND fail to rethrow, call the sink, or return a value that carries the cause. Kind: Roslyn syntax-node analyzer on CatchClauseSyntax. Group 4's own acceptance check 9 only greps this once and does not hold it afterwards, and this is the class-level guard for CLAUDE.md rule 1. A SuppressMessage with Tim's sign-off is the interim exception path, as already used for CA1031.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: Re-introducing a swallowed catch like the thirteen found. The existing CA1031 suppressions already hide sanctioned catches, which is the audit's gap.

rulesToAdd.rule: Loaded<T>.Why must be read only by an approved reporter (the sink call sites). Any other read of .Why, or construction of Loaded<T> with Why set to a non-constant that includes an absolute project path, is flagged. Optional and lower priority: it is only worth building if the first rule's allow-list proves too coarse to cover Why.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: A third consumer starts forwarding Why into a user-visible or agent-visible field, widening the one new type's reach beyond what Tim approved.

risks: The contract's group 3 text says FileGuard 383-387 'carries the exception's message into Verdict.Deny'. That contradicts decision `tell`. I resolved it for `tell` (message to the sink, fixed Deny text) but the contract text should be corrected, and Tim should be told which way it went.

FileGuard already returns CaptureFailed with exception.Message and the file path (lines 95-99, 192-196, 221-225). If CaptureFailed's reason is shown to the agent, the 'no raw exception text, no absolute path' requirement is ALREADY violated in the live code and acceptance 8a would fail on those paths. I have not traced where CaptureFailed is rendered, so the worker must do that before relying on 8a.

The warning sink is itself a new type that is approved but not yet built, and group 3 depends on group 4 delivering it. Ordering inside the single piece of work must put the sink first. Ed25519SignatureService sits in Boundaries, below Engine, so a sink reachable from there may not exist without an upward dependency. If not, one Verify catch cannot report its cause, and that needs Tim's decision.

A corrupt or wrong-length grant key now raises at composition (decision `trust`), which can stop a whole pipeline from starting where it used to run with grants disabled. That is the intent, but it is a behaviour change that the contract's 'never changes whether anything denies' line sits uneasily beside. Existing tests that pass a short key (GrantStore.Create currently coerces it to Empty) need rechecking.

IGrantStore is an approved contract interface. Changing its return type breaks every fake and test implementation, and the analyzers that pin the contract surface (ContractPublicSurfaceMustMatchInterface, NoClassInAbstractions) must accept a record in Abstractions. NoClassInAbstractions in particular may reject the new record, and I have not checked it. The worker must run the analyzers early.

GrantStore continuing to report to the sink on every call could be noisy, since GetActiveGrantsAsync runs per write. Dedupe is not designed here, and adding one would be a new mechanism that needs approval.

approach: VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE CODE. (a) Member shape: a new contract interface `IWarningSink` in src/AgentGuard.Abstractions/Contracts with ONE member, `void Warn(string message)`, exposed on ISystemServices as `IWarningSink Warnings { get; }`. It mirrors the sibling IConsole (sync, string in, void out; IConsole.ErrorWriteLine is the same shape) and mirrors the primitive, not policy (memory: feedback-abstraction-mirrors-primitive-not-policy). It returns void and takes no severity or category, so it is the sink Tim approved ("Give it one place to go") and no more. No new exception, result or logging type. The ISystemServices root rule AG0034 accepts it (a property whose value type is a Contracts interface). (b) Owner: the adapter lives in AgentGuard.Boundaries beside ConsoleAdapter/EnvironmentAdapter (owners-live-at-lowest-consumer; internal sealed, private ctor, static Create), built by hand in SystemServices.Create (src/AgentGuard.Engine/SystemServices.cs:104-125) which gets one more ctor parameter, and the SystemServices ctor/property pair. Tests: SystemServicesBuilder (tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers) gets a `Slot<IWarningSink>`, `With(IWarningSink)`, `Wrap(...)` and a RecordingWarningSink fake, because AG0019 (BuilderCompletenessAnalyzer) mirrors the container against the builder and fails the build otherwise. (c) Where the CLI lands it: the adapter writes ONE line to standard error, `agentguard: warning - <message>`, through the same owned console channel the CLI already uses for `agentguard: failing closed - ...` (Program.cs:200) and for execution.Message (Program.cs:189). The CLI (Program.Run -> SystemServices.Create()) is the only place that composes the container, so it is where the sink's destination is chosen; stdout is NOT used because the hook's stdout/exit code is the host protocol (HostDecision). Exit code and verdict are untouched, so a failed sweep never blocks a call. The adapter must not swallow its own failure: if the stderr write throws, it propagates. (d) PrivilegedWriter: it does NOT stop at the first failed effect and does NOT aggregate into an exception or result. Both the IPrivilegedWriter doc ("one effect's failure does not abort the rest") and the class doc already say best-effort-continue, and throwing would be caught by Pipeline.RunPostAsync's catch-all and turned into Verdict.Deny, changing allow/deny, which the contract forbids ("Group 3 changes what a denial says, never whether it is made" and group 4's keep-running decision). So: keep the foreach; replace the two empty catches with one `catch (Exception e) when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)` that calls `_warnings.Warn($"Could not {restore|delete} '{path}': {e.Message}")` once per failed effect and continues; cancellation still propagates. Per-effect warning means a restore that fails is named individually, which aggregation into one message would only blur. The signature stays `Task ExecuteAsync(...)`; PrivilegedWriter.Create(ISystemServices) already draws services from the container (PrivilegedWriter.cs:59) so it adds `services.Warnings` with no new parameter. (e) Pipeline: it already holds `_services` (Pipeline.cs:25,30), so SweepBestEffortAsync (lines 174-188) and DeleteBestEffortAsync (190-204) call `_services.Warnings.Warn(...)` in their catch and continue; no verdict is involved and no restructuring of RunPreAsync/RunPostAsync is needed. This is why the sink works where Verdict.Warn cannot: GROUND found no verdict exists at either point. Those two methods are the same shape (a try around one store call, same two catches), so they collapse into ONE private helper taking the store call and a one-line description; PrivilegedWriter's filter and the two Pipeline copies share the IOException-or-UnauthorizedAccessException test, which should be one internal Engine predicate rather than three copies of the pair (DRY). (f) PosixFileSystem.TryRemoveLink does NOT use the sink. It sits in AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.MacOS, below the container: PlatformServices.Create() takes no arguments and runs BEFORE SystemServices exists (SystemServices.cs:104), and handing a service down into it is both a one-way-dependency violation (memory: dependencies-point-one-way) and an AG0031 service-as-parameter. So the per-OS adapters raise, exactly as the contract's group 4 says: at the second call site (line 70, immediately before the IOException with errno) the cleanup failure is folded into that exception as its message plus InnerException; at the first call site (line 64, pre-clearing a unique random temporary sibling) the delete is called plainly and any failure propagates, so TryRemoveLink and its two empty catches are deleted entirely. The same edit lands in the Linux build through the csproj link (AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Linux.csproj:30). Windows has no TryRemoveLink. THE CONTRACT SENTENCE 'so the per-OS adapters are covered' IS THEREFORE NOT LITERALLY TRUE for the sink and Tim should be told plainly; the per-OS adapters are covered by raising, and by the callers in Engine that hold the sink.

rulesToAdd.rule: No comment-only or empty catch block anywhere in src/ or tests/ (a catch whose body holds no statement). A catch must rethrow, wrap and throw, call a sink, return a reason, or assert. Analyzer kind: Roslyn syntax-node analyzer (CatchClauseSyntax whose Block has no statements), severity Warning-as-error like the rest of AgentGuard.Architecture; a [SuppressMessage] is the existing interim exception path, Tim-approved only.
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: The exact class this contract cleans: an AI (or tired human) silences a failure with `catch { // best-effort }`. Today it is caught only by acceptance check 9, a Python regex run once; the tree has no analyzer, EDITORCONFIG rule, S108/S2486 setting or CA1031 coverage for it (verified by grep), so the next best-effort cleanup reintroduces the defect and nothing fails the build. NOTE: contract says 'Rules to add: None', so this needs Tim's yes before RULE-PHASE; it is raised because the rule trigger says a rule is developed whenever one can be.

rulesToAdd.rule: Only the one warning-sink owner and its call sites may be reached for 'report and continue': an analyzer pinning IWarningSink.Warn calls to a catch clause (or to a method that the contract names) so the sink cannot become a general logger or a way to demote a failure that should stop the call. Kind: Roslyn invocation analyzer. Lower value than rule 1; offered only if Tim wants the sink's 'stops nothing' meaning enforced, since a Warn in a non-catch position is the likeliest misuse (using Warn instead of Deny).
rulesToAdd.failureModeStopped: Warn used as a softer substitute for raising or denying (laundering a shortcut as a choice), which would convert future fail-closed sites into silent warnings.

risks: The contract says the sink 'covers the per-OS adapters'. It cannot: PlatformServices.Create() runs before the container exists and takes no arguments; injecting the sink down is a one-way-dependency violation and AG0031. The per-OS adapters (PosixFileSystem) raise instead. Tim must be told this plainly; it does not change his decision text ('behind ISystemServices ... the command line decides where it lands') but it changes what 'covered' means.

Visibility: Claude Code does not show a hook's stderr on exit 0 to the model, only in verbose/transcript mode, so a warning on stderr is seen by Tim, not the guarded agent. That matches the approved 'coarse to it, exact to you' rule, but it means the warning is quiet unless someone looks at the hook log. No alternative surface is approved; do not fold the warning into Verdict.Warn at Pre (a Warn renders to the agent via HostDecision and could leak a path).

The sink adapter writes to the console. Building it from IConsole inside SystemServices.Create could trip AG0031 (service as a method parameter) or AG0016 (raw System.Console allowed only in ConsoleAdapter). If the analyzers refuse, the clean fallback is for ConsoleAdapter to also implement IWarningSink (one class, two interfaces; check AG0005 and container-interface-single-owner), NOT a rule-dodging shape. Treat a block as a wall, stop and report.

If the sink's own stderr write throws (closed pipe), the exception escapes the catch; in Pipeline the sweep is inside RunPreAsync's try so it becomes a Deny. That is loud but means a broken stderr blocks calls. Alternative would be swallowing it, which the project rule forbids; I chose loud and recommend Tim confirm.

A new ISystemServices member changes every container implementer: SystemServices, the test builder's nested container and any fake implementing ISystemServices, and the seven container-walking analyzers' tests. The group 2 test (resolve ISystemServices from the live assembly) should be written and RED-checked first so a broken resolve is not mistaken for this change.

Pipeline's DeleteBestEffortAsync runs in finally after the verdict is chosen, so the warning arrives after the verdict is computed; this is fine because the sink is a side channel, and is the reason a Verdict.Warn would not work.

Exception filter `when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)` narrows what was caught before only if the order changes nothing; confirm DirectoryNotFoundException (an IOException) still warns on the post-delete path rather than being silently expected.

approach: One new test class in analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests (LiveContainerResolvesTests.cs) that builds a compilation from the LIVE source of src/AgentGuard.Abstractions and runs BoundaryServices.ResolveTree over it. Chosen over a ProjectReference/assembly reference because the runner compiles against net9.0 reference assemblies (AnalyzerRunner.ResolveReferencesAsync, Net90) while src/AgentGuard.Abstractions builds net10.0 (Directory.Build.props:13), so a built-DLL reference risks a version-mismatch error; parsing the source avoids it, needs no new csproj edge, and reads the file the contract line 60 and 119 name. Repo-root lookup reuses the existing RepositoryFiles.FindRepositoryRoot (RepositoryFiles.cs:25), already used by four sibling tests. Verified facts: ResolveTree returns null exactly when WellKnownType.Resolve cannot find AgentGuard.Abstractions.Contracts.ISystemServices (BoundaryServices.cs:52-63); WellKnownType.Resolve searches the merged namespace tree, so it finds the type whether it is declared in the compilation or in a referenced assembly (WellKnownType.cs:120-168). Test shape (three facts, all failing loudly with Assert.NotNull and a message naming the path and the seven analyzers): (1) Live_ISystemServices_ResolvesToATree: compile the live Abstractions sources as the assembly under analysis, call ResolveTree, Assert.NotNull. (2) Live_ISystemServices_ResolvesFromAReferencedAssembly: compile the live sources as a separate assembly named AgentGuard.Abstractions and reference it from a bare consumer compilation, then Assert.NotNull on ResolveTree of the consumer. This is AG0034's second case (container declared only in a referenced assembly), so the fence covers both ways the container reaches a compilation and cannot break that case; both compile modes go through one new AnalyzerRunner helper that takes a list of source texts, because CompileAsync and RunWithReferenceAsync take one string today. The helper keeps ThrowOnUnexpectedCompilerErrors, so a live tree the net9 references cannot compile fails loudly rather than being skipped (CLAUDE.md rule 1). (3) Live_Tree_MatchesTheHandWrittenRealShapeContainer: assert BoundaryServices.Resolve and ContainerInterfaces over the live compilation equal the same over SharedAnalyzerSources.RealShapeContainer (ServiceInterfaces, ServiceTypes, container triple). This is what closes the drift gap the angle names: today nothing parses the real container, so RealShapeContainer can drift with every test green; with fact 3 any added or removed service on the real ISystemServices turns a test red until the copy is updated. The live sources are enumerated with Directory.EnumerateFiles over src/AgentGuard.Abstractions, **/*.cs, excluding obj and bin path segments, and the test also asserts the enumeration is non-empty (an empty folder must fail, not yield a null tree that reads as a pass of nothing). No production code, no analyzer change, no new rule. One real fence, one place: the seven inert analyzers are not individually tested, because they all read the single ResolveTree null, so one test covers all seven (DRY).

approach:
Group 5 and the test-cleanup half of group 4, each change made in the one place that already owns the job, and each one backed by something that fails if the silence returns. All of it was checked against the live tree.

1. ci.yml uploads. Change the three evidence uploads from warn to error (ci.yml lines 127, 258, 381; macos is included because the defect class is the same, which is the scope-by-behavior rule). The six signed-artifact uploads are already error. The existing guard, EvidenceUploadsCannotRegressTests in analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests, parses ci.yml and its ConformanceProblems does not check if-no-files-found. The test's own conforming fixture, ConformanceProblems_AcceptsAConformingEvidenceUpload, carries `if-no-files-found: warn` and would pin the old value. So extend ConformanceProblems to require `error`, and move that fixture to `error`. This is tightening a test, and the contract says an existing test may not be weakened or re-pointed, so the change is flagged for approval in risks. The upload runs with if: always(), so on a leg that fails before producing files it now also goes red. That leg was already red; only the reported cause changes.

2. check-copied-modules.mjs. Add a step "Copied modules" to the typescript job, which already runs on three OSes (ci.yml:424). It runs from the repo root, which the script needs because it reads process.cwd()/.agents/workflows, so no working-directory override is needed. Give the repo a package.json script `check:modules` that runs `node eng/check-copied-modules.mjs`, and have the CI step call that script. It has no skip path: it exits 1 on drift or unbalanced markers. The ground.js comment at line 1307 claims enforcement that did not exist, and this step makes it true. Record in docs/silent-failure-audit.md that tsc and eslint still do not cover .agents/workflows/*.js, because those scripts move to TypeScript under #58.

3. eslint.config.js. The probe in the GROUND facts shows that with both no-unsafe-* rules on, exactly one violation appears across the 32 files linted: ts/metalang/kit.test.ts:97 (no-unsafe-member-access). There are zero no-unsafe-assignment violations. So the premise "the files that narrow YAML" is false in the live tree. Replace the global off block with a block scoped by `files: ['ts/metalang/kit.test.ts']`, turning off only no-unsafe-member-access, and rewrite the comment to say what is true. Acceptance 12 ("names each file, no directory glob") holds. Before the narrowing is final I would re-run the probe with `bun run lint`. Fixing the one site in kit.test.ts with a narrow instead of a disable is better still. That is a code fix inside a file the contract names, but it departs from the contract's wording, so it goes to the contract author rather than being taken by the worker.

4. local-cosign.sh and local-cosign.ps1. All three skips become non-zero exits, each naming its condition: the switch being off, running in CI, and no interactive terminal. Nothing in the build calls these scripts (only eng/signing/README.md mentions them), so the nonzero exits break no pipeline. Update README.md:34-37, which says "Unset it is a no-op", to say it now exits non-zero by design. In the .ps1, also check $LASTEXITCODE after `cosign sign-blob` (line 37), because a failed native call falls through to the "Wrote ..." message today; the .sh already has set -euo pipefail. Distinct exit codes per skip (for example 3, 4, 5) let a caller tell them apart; they are folded into one shared message table if the two scripts can use one, but the two scripts are different languages so each keeps its own, with README as the single list of codes.

5. version.compute.targets:81,86. The MSBuild copy has no CI guard; the CI-side mirror eng/compute-build-id.sh:19-25 does. Mirror that exactly. After the git Exec, add an <Error> task with Condition `'$(_AgHash)' == 'local'` combined with CI detection: `'$(CI)' != '' or '$(GITHUB_ACTIONS)' != ''`, matching the shell test of CI or GITHUB_OUTPUT. A local build keeps stamping `local` (Tim's decision `local`). Detecting CI the same way in both halves is the "the two halves agree" requirement. Acceptance 10a and 10b are proven by running `dotnet msbuild -t:AgentGuardComputeCore` with PATH stripped of git, once with CI unset and once with CI=true.

6. win-arm64 and linux-x64 legs. The contract allows either running the tests or recording why the leg stays build-only. GROUND found a Rosetta precedent on macOS (AGENTGUARD_EXPECT_ARCH=X64) but no x64-on-arm precedent for Windows or Linux. Recommendation: do not invent new runners. Record both legs in docs/silent-failure-audit.md as build-only with the reason (the runner is the other architecture, and signing is push-only), and make the step names say so. The one exception worth taking now: ubuntu-24.04-arm can run linux-x64 binaries only through emulation, so a cheap smoke test `--version` of the published x64 binary under qemu is not recommended without Tim's yes. If Tim wants the legs to run tests, that is a new job and goes through approval. This choice is flagged, not made by the design.

7. Test-cleanup catches, at the real paths: tests/Shared/TestTempDirectory.cs:23-37, tests/AgentGuard.Tests/SetupHarness.cs:207-223, tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/FixtureProject.cs, tests/AgentGuard.Tests/CliMachine.cs and tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/PlatformFileSystemSpecTests.cs:302. The same IOException plus UnauthorizedAccessException pair is written out separately in eight places. Per DRY, TestTempDirectory.DeleteBestEffort is the existing owner for deleting a real temp directory. Route FixtureProject and CliMachine to it (verify with grep that they delete real directories and not the overlay), and delete the catch rather than copying it. SetupHarness deletes on the in-memory overlay, where an IOException means a real bug, so the catch is removed and the exception surfaces. The PlatformFileSystemSpecTests.cs:302 catch of DirectoryNotFoundException ("Nothing to clean up") swallows a benign case, but it is the same shape. Replace it with an Exists check before the delete, so the benign case is handled by a visible condition and anything else surfaces. Delete the stale worktree copies under .claude/worktrees only if Tim says so; they are outside the live tree and outside acceptance check 9's `src tests` scope.

8. Acceptance 9. The contract already replaced the single-line grep with a multi-line Python regex. Keep it, but make it permanent: see the rules below, so the regex runs on every test run instead of once in the worker's transcript.
